title: Private Deployments — VPC & On‑Prem: Comprehensive Deployment, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document is the canonical Redwood reference for Private Deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It consolidates reference architectures, packaging and installation notes, an operational Day‑2 playbook, and prescriptive upgrade/rollback procedures. Use this guide for customer-facing deployments and internal runbook authoring.

Audience:
- Solutions engineers and platform operators performing initial deployments.
- SREs and customer Ops teams responsible for Day‑2 operations, upgrades, and incident triage.
- Security and compliance reviewers validating private deployment requirements.

Scope and intent:
- Supported deployment modes: VPC-hosted private control plane with customer network peering, and fully on‑prem (air‑gapped) packaging.
- Components covered: control plane, serving runtime, model-store, observability stack, secrets/KMS integration, and optional cache/batch tiers.
- Not covered: detailed application integration (SDK usage) — see eng-developer-experience docs.

1) Architectural overview
Provide a concise diagram (textual) and component list:
- Control plane (Redwood Private API + Console) — optional external access for metrics/rollouts or run in customer-managed namespace for fully isolated deployments.
- Serving runtime (inference workers) — GPU-backed pods/hosts with KV cache and batching service.
- Model store (artifact repository) — S3-compatible object store (minio) or cloud bucket.
- State & metadata DB — PostgreSQL (primary) with read replicas for dashboards.
- Observability — Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, and traces (Jaeger/OTel).
- Service mesh / ingress — optional (Istio/Contour) depending on customer networking.

Reference architectures (examples)
- Small (PoC / single-customer dev):
  - 1 control-plane replica, 2 inference workers (single GPU), minio single node, PostgreSQL single instance
  - Use case: cost-constrained evaluation, non-prod traffic

- Medium (production, single AZ):
  - 3 control-plane replicas, 4 inference workers (N GPUs across hosts), minio HA, PostgreSQL primary + standby, Prometheus + Grafana HA
  - Use case: SMB customer with steady throughput and SLA ~99.5%

- Enterprise (multi-AZ, high-availability):
  - 5 control-plane replicas, autoscaling inference pool across AZs, object store replicated, DB cluster with failover, multi-region telemetry backends, and cross-region fallback routing
  - Use case: regulated customers with strict uptime and data residency needs

Minimum hardware and sizing guidance table (textual):
| Component | Minimum (PoC) | Recommended (Prod) | Notes |
| Control plane | 2 vCPU, 8GB RAM | 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM x3 replicas | For heavy console usage, increase replicas |
| Inference worker | 1x A100/RTX6000 equivalent | Cluster of GPUs (scale to qps) | Match model memory and kv-cache needs |
| Model store | 100GB | Depends on model catalog | Use lifecycle policies for cold storage |
| DB | 2 vCPU, 8GB | Managed Postgres or 4 vCPU, 16GB | Ensure WAL shipping/backups |

2) Pre-deployment checklist
- Customer sign-offs: network topology diagram, IP ranges, firewall rules, and compliance requirements.
- Networking: ensure CIDR allocations, routing, DNS, outbound egress policy for updates (unless air-gapped), and required ports open (see Ports & Endpoints section).
- Credentials: KMS integration keys, service account for deployment, S3 credentials for model artifacts.
- Quota checks: GPU capacity, storage, load balancer quotas.
- Backups & retention: validated backup plan for DB and model-store.

Ports & endpoints (essential)
- Control plane API: 443 (HTTPS)
- Inference worker gRPC: 7070 (internal)
- Metrics scrape: Prometheus 9090, exporters 9100
- Internal storage access: S3 endpoints (customer bucket/minio)

3) Packaging & installation patterns
Supported installers:
- Helm charts (Kubernetes) — primary installation pattern for VPC/on‑prem K8s.
- Docker Compose / systemd bundles — for small or air‑gapped single-host installs.
- Air-gapped installer — tarball with container images, manifests, and offline package index.

Helm installation quickstart (example values):
```yaml
# values.yaml (example excerpt)
replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: registry.redwood-inference/internal/private
  tag: v2027.01.0
modelStore:
  type: s3
  endpoint: https://minio.local
  bucket: redwood-models
kafka:
  enabled: false # optional, depends on eventing needs
resources:
  controlPlane:
    requests:
      cpu: "500m"
      memory: "1Gi"
    limits:
      cpu: "2"
      memory: "4Gi"
```

Air-gapped install notes:
- Provide container images as OCI tarball (registry mirror) and include an offline CRD/manifest package.
- Ensure KMS/secret injection method works without external network calls (e.g., local HSM integration or pre-provisioned credentials).

Packaging policy and image signing:
- All release images are signed with our internal sigstore key. For air-gapped installs, include signature bundle and signing public key with the offline package.

4) Day-2 operations (runbook highlights)
Monitoring & alerting (SLOs & key alerts):
- SLOs:
  - API latency p50/p95: 50ms / 300ms (control-plane)
  - Inference tail latency p99: target depends on model, default <= 2s for small models
  - Availability: 99.5% for Dedicated customers, configurable for Private deployments
- Alerts to configure:
  - Heartbeats missing (control-plane pod count mismatch)
  - Rising model load queue (> configurable threshold)
  - Prometheus node exporter down
  - Model fetch errors > 5% for 5 minutes

Routine maintenance tasks:
1. Weekly: rotate short-lived certs, check disk usage on model-store nodes, validate backups.
2. Monthly: run canary prompts through rev-proxy, run model quality smoke tests, review rollout windows.
3. Quarterly: capacity planning review and test failover drills.

Scaling guidance:
- Autoscaler settings: set CPU/GPU-based autoscaling policies with a safety buffer of 20% above observed peak.
- Warm pools: keep a small warm pool of idle inference workers to reduce cold-start latency for larger models.

5) Upgrade procedure (recommended rolling upgrade)
Pre-upgrade checks:
- Verify backups are successful (DB & model-store) and retention policy is intact.
- Ensure customer has approved maintenance window and rollback criteria.
- Confirm health endpoints are green and no active critical alerts.

Canary rollout steps:
1. Deploy control-plane update to 1 replica (canary) with monitoring hooks enabled.
2. Run smoke tests: API health, basic inference for 3 canonical prompts, model fetch test.
3. If canary passes (no errors for 15 minutes), advance to 20% of replicas for 10 minutes.
4. Gradually increase to 100% using rollout policy (maxUnavailable=1, maxSurge=1).

Verification checklist after upgrade:
- SLO checks (p95/p99) compared to baseline.
- Model-serving correctness via automated prompt set (quality regression checks).
- Telemetry sanity: no spike in error rates, traces correlate with expected latency.

6) Rollback procedure (fast fallback)
When to rollback:
- Canary failure: functional regression or repeated errors within canary window.
- Production degradation: sustained SLO violations > configurable threshold (e.g., p99 latency increase > 2x and error rate >2%).

Rollback steps (Kubernetes Helm example):
1. Immediately mark the new release as paused in deployment tool (e.g., ArgoCD pause or kubectl rollout pause).
2. Revert to the previous image tag via helm rollback or kubectl set image to prior tag.
3. Scale up previous replicas if required and wait for readiness (readiness probes green).
4. Run sanity tests (same smoke tests used in canary).
5. Postmortem: capture logs, traces, and the failing request samples; open an incident and assign to oncall/serving-runtime owner.

7) Troubleshooting & known failure modes
- Model fetch timeouts: check S3 endpoint network ACLs and model-store health; restart minio if needed.
- GPU OOMs at inference worker: verify model memory footprint, enable quantized profile or increase GPU memory.
- DB connection saturation: add read replicas and scale connection pool; check max_connections and use PgBouncer.

8) Customer requirements library (checklists & templates)
Networking & connectivity checklist:
- Allowed outbound endpoints (if not air‑gapped): registry.redwood-inference (for updates), telemetry endpoints, object-store endpoints.
- Inbound rules: control-plane API load-balancer IPs and ports.

Security & compliance checklist:
- Required: TLS for all external endpoints, RBAC for console access, KMS/HSM integration for model keys.
- Optional: FIPS-enabled crypto, signed container image verification, audit log forwarding to customer SIEM.

Data residency & retention templates:
- Provide sample retention policy statements (e.g., retention 90 days for logs, 365 days for audit records) and sample S3 lifecycle rules.

9) Ownership, escalation, and runbook links
- Primary owners:
  - eng-private-deployments (oncall): pager duty team: #redwood-private-oncall
  - eng-serving-runtime: model serving incidents and regressions
  - eng-platform: orchestration and autoscaler issues

Escalation matrix (high level):
1. L1: oncall engineer (eng-private-deployments) — initial triage and mitigation
2. L2: eng-serving-runtime owner — performance regressions
3. L3: engineering leadership and SRE for major outages

Runbook links (internal):
- private-deployments-deployment-runbook
- private-deployments-day2-upgrade-rollback
- private-deployments-vpc-onprem-operational-guide

10) Change history
- 2026-10-05: created by Aisha Patel (initial consolidation).
- 2026-12-15: added air‑gapped packaging and image-signing policy.
- 2027-01-25: updated upgrade/rollback windows and SLO targets after field feedback.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting commands (examples)
- Check control-plane pods: kubectl get pods -n redwood-control-plane
- Run model fetch test: curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/model/fetch -d '{"model":"small-gpt"}'
- Verify DB backups: pg_dump --list or check backup job in backup namespace

Notes and references:
- See eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-vpc-onprem-reference-architectures-packaging-day2-ops-2028.json for extended packaging policy.
- For SDK integration and prod prompts, see eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates.
